messages:
sarah: Hey team — after upgrading our service to the latest python SDK (1.31.0) we started seeing authorization failures and duplicate charges. Was working on 1.30.2.

sarah: Quick repro: simple call to client.generate with bearer token. Intermittent 401 on first attempt, then client retries and we see 2 successful requests billed.

sarah: Repro snippet:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(token=os.getenv('RW_TOKEN'))
res = client.generate(model='redwood-v1', prompt='hi')
print(res.text)
```

dev-support: thanks, can you paste exact header logs (with token redacted) and confirm which retry policy you're using?

sarah: logs (sanitized):
```
REQ -> POST /v1/generate headers={Authorization: Bearer ***** , Idempotency-Key: None}
RESP <- 401 Unauthorized
REQ -> POST /v1/generate headers={Authorization: Bearer ***** , Idempotency-Key: 3f2b-...}
RESP <- 200 OK
```

sarah: We're not setting idempotency keys; expecting SDK to attach one for idempotent requests. This started after SDK upgrade.

ajay: fwiw we changed default idempotency behavior in 1.31 — internal note: removed automatic idempotency key for short-lived tokens to avoid leaking scope. Looks like that change interacts badly with transient 401s + retry.

ajay: can you confirm token type? (service key vs user token)

sarah: it's a service key (long-lived). We only started seeing duplicates when the auth check returned a 401 transiently (token validation race on our side). Before 1.31 SDK would retry with same idempotency-key so server deduped. Now retry sends second request without idempotency key, so billed twice.

emma: digging into the SDK change — release note says: "don't attach idempotency-key automatically when token scope unknown". That was intended for multi-tenant flows but we didn't account for the common service-key workflow.

emma: short-term workaround: pin to 1.30.2 or explicitly set idempotency key on the request:
```python
client.generate(..., idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()))
```

liam: can you confirm whether setting REDWOOD_AUTH_SCOPE env var helps as a workaround?

sarah: tried REDWOOD_AUTH_SCOPE=upload:generate — still saw a few failures but much reduced. Not ideal.

dev-support: i'll escalate to engineering and billing. billing-bot: flagging potential duplicate charges for customer acct: acct-12345 — please review. :rotating_light:

billing-bot: Billing team notified, creating case #BILL-2026-78.

emma: assigned to me. Plan: revert the idempotency gating logic for service-key flows in a patch (1.31.1) and add a safety net that forces idempotency-key on retry when server responds 401/5xx. I'll post a PR and a rollout timeline.

emma: immediate action: recommend pin to 1.30.2 for affected customers, or set explicit idempotency_key on calls. We'll aim to cut 1.31.1 today if no blockers.

sarah: thanks — high priority for us, traffic spike caused unexpected billing.

liam: thx — keep us posted. If you need us to pause customer billing ingestion for that account while you patch, ping billing-bot with the case id.

deploy-bot: Release pipeline triggered for branch fix/idempotency-servicekey (CI: 12 checks).

emma: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/789 (WIP) — will update when merged. :rocket:

sarah: appreciated.

dev-support: marking thread resolved when patch is released and customer confirms billing adjustment. :thumbsup:
